slides.heading: Powerset
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Powerset, a medium recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Every subset of a set of distinct ints (iteratively doubling).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Every subset of a set of distinct ints (iteratively doubling).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Each new element doubles the subsets: every existing subset with or without it.
slides.narration: Each new element doubles the subsets: every existing subset with or without it.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Bitmask: each of 2ⁿ masks picks a subset
O(n · 2ⁿ) time and space either way
slides.narration: Each subset corresponds to an n-bit mask, so there are two to the n of them. Iteratively doubling the list, or recursion, produces them all in n times two to the n.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each element, copy all subsets and add it
slides.narration: Step by step. First, start with the empty set. Second, for each element, copy all subsets and add it. Third, return all.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Start with the empty set
slides.narration: Start with just the empty subset.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After 1: 2 subsets
slides.narration: For 1, copy every existing subset and add 1 to the copy. That doubles the count to 2.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After 2: 4 subsets
slides.narration: For 2, copy every existing subset and add 2 to the copy. That doubles the count to 4.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After 3: 8 subsets
slides.narration: For 3, copy every existing subset and add 3 to the copy. That doubles the count to 8.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We start with one empty subset. For each value, we take the current size and, for each existing subset, add a copy with the value appended.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times 2 to the n. Space is O of n times 2 to the n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Capture the list size before the inner loop, or you'll loop forever on subsets you just added. Remember the empty set.

bullets: Follow-up: subsets with duplicates, subsets summing to k
slides.narration: Mention the bitmask view. Follow-ups handle duplicates or restrict to a target sum.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Each new element doubles the subsets: every existing subset with or without it.
slides.narration: To recap Powerset: Each new element doubles the subsets: every existing subset with or without it. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
